item.title: 'CRISPR-Combo' system speeds regeneration of hard-to-breed perennial crops
item.description: Editing a plant's genes is only half the battle. Before a new, improved trait can ever reach a farmer's field, scientists must be able to grow a whole plant from just a few edited cells—a process that can be slow, unreliable and, for some plant species, impossible. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Portland report maps complex journeys through homelessness
item.description: A new report from Portland State University's Homelessness Research and Action Collaborative (HRAC) and the OHSU-PSU School of Public Health offers an in-depth examination of how individuals navigate, survive and attempt to exit homelessness in Multnomah County. Titled "Without a Map: A Lived Experience Study of the Paths People Create Through Homelessness," the publication serves as the second and final part of the Pathways study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: The Republic of Djibouti will sign the Artemis Accords during a ceremony at 11 a.m. EDT, Monday, Sept. 14, at NASA Headquarters in Washington, becoming the 72nd country signatory. NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson will host Ambassador of Djibouti to the United States Mohamed Siad Douale for the ceremony, together with U.S. State Department Assistant […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: New genomic tool for clams boosts sustainable aquaculture
item.description: An international team of researchers, including CIIMAR, has developed a new tool that could help produce clams that are more resistant to disease and climate change while also strengthening the conservation of these species' genetic diversity. The study, published in the journal Aquaculture, represents a significant step forward for sustainable aquaculture and the management of two of the most economically important clam species: the Japanese clam (Ruditapes philippinarum) and the good clam (Ruditapes decussatus). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global study reveals hidden nutritional value of shellfish and other aquatic invertebrates
item.description: The nutritional value of aquatic invertebrates such as oysters, mussels and crabs has been significantly overlooked, according to a new study led by researchers at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST). The findings provide one of the most comprehensive assessments to date of the nutritional contribution of aquatic invertebrates, along with new evidence to better understand their role in human nutrition and help inform more sustainable fisheries, aquaculture and food-system planning. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Katie Miller held a large stake in Elon Musk’s AI company as she bashed its rivals online: report
item.description: Miller defended her stake and said she was not being paid to digitally promote Musk’s company, which has skyrocketed in value in recent months Fuente: The Independent - World.
item.dc:creator: Josh Marcus

item.title: Unveiling how nanoparticles create iridescence in ancient ceramics
item.description: Scientists led by the Universitat Politècnica de Barcelona and the ESRF, the European Synchrotron, have revealed the chemical reactions in nanoparticles that created a unique, shimmering effect in the painting on ninth-century Islamic ceramics. The results are published in Science Advances. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How sex with multiple mates can help save species from extinction
item.description: Allowing females to mate with multiple males, rather than just one, could help make species more resistant to extinction, University of East Anglia research shows. A new study reveals that when females have multiple males to mate with, their offspring inherit significantly fewer harmful genetic mutations. This, in turn, makes the entire population healthier and less likely to die out. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Supercomputer simulations reveal how the molecular motor kinesin steers itself along tracks
item.description: Kinesin is a molecular motor responsible for hauling essential cargoes within cells by walking step by step along filamentous tracks known as microtubules. To move efficiently and avoid falling off, the motor's two feet must coordinate their stepping in a precise direction. Scientists have known that a connecting segment called the neck region is crucial for coordinating this motion. However, its exact three-dimensional structure and how it physically interacts with the microtubule track have remained a mystery because of the limitations of current imaging techniques. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Answers President’s Call to Establish United States Space Academy
item.description: Less than two weeks after an Executive Order was signed to create the first United States Space Academy, NASA-led work is in full swing to make the academy a reality and shape the future of America’s aerospace workforce and leadership. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman chaired the first Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Lauren E. Low

item.title: Ancient Swedish Goths had surprisingly accurate calendars
item.description: On a mostly flat plain an hour north of Stockholm lies a collection of large burial mounds dating from an ancient culture at least 2,500 years old. These people were not Vikings; they were northern Germanic Goths, pagan polytheists worshiping the precursors of Odin, Freyr and Thor. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: An unusual bacterium that penetrates and lives inside human cells may offer a new drug target
item.description: Research underway in the lab of Rebecca Alexander, a professor in Wake Forest University's Department of Chemistry, is shedding light on an unusual human bacterium, Mycoplasma penetrans. Alexander's work to understand how and why this unique pathogen acts as it does could one day lead to new classes of drugs that better target illnesses associated with this particular pathogen, as well as others that act similarly. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Life-Saving Technology Where Cell Signals Can’t Go
item.description: Search and rescue technology developed in part by NASA saved five lives Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Wagner

item.title: What small insects can tell us about ancient textiles
item.description: Anna Sheinberg, Ph.D. candidate in chemistry, is working with fellow researchers in Trinity College's Chemistry Department and at the Nasher Museum of Art to uncover new information about some of the ancient dyed textiles in the Nasher's collection. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rethinking how household income needs are assessed for welfare support
item.description: How much more income does a two-person household need than a person living alone? The answer is not simply twice as much. Two people need more food and other necessities, but they can also share expenses such as housing. This means that as a household grows, the income needed to maintain the same standard of living increases—but usually by less than the number of people in the household. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: From flower to fruit: A tug-of-war between growing tissues
item.description: Unlike an animal cell, a plant cell can't crawl or migrate. It's locked inside a rigid wall, cemented to its neighbors for life. A cell born at the center of a young fruit will still be there when that fruit ripens. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Climate hazards disrupted schooling for more than 171 million students in 2025
item.description: More than 171 million students globally—or 1 in 10—from preprimary to upper secondary age had their schooling disrupted by climate hazards in 2025, according to a new analysis released by UNICEF today. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Kids' brains are built for distraction. Sometimes that's a good thing.
item.description: Parents often learn the hard way that to make it anywhere on time, they should calculate how much time they think they need to get ready—and double it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tightly guided atoms could enable low-power quantum navigation when GPS fails
item.description: Within tiny halos of light clinging to a vanishingly thin wisp of optical fiber, scientist Jongmin Lee guides atoms like marbles through a narrow pipe. Rock the fiber and the atoms shift side by side; they just don't fall off. But don't be deceived by the seemingly delicate nature of his experiment. Lee is exploring how to measure motion precisely in rough-and-tumble environments. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First PLP-dependent enzyme that influences bacterial protein production discovered
item.description: Researchers from the Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research & Technology's (SMART) Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) interdisciplinary research group, alongside collaborators from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Nanyang Technological University (NTU Singapore), and institutions in the United States, Poland and France, have discovered aminovaleramididine synthetase (AvaS), the first identified pyridoxal phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme responsible for producing a chemical modification linked to how bacteria respond to metabolic stress. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Europe will go it alone on Venus mission after NASA yanks radar instrument
item.description: Europe is looking inward, and perhaps to China, as the White House tries to cancel some NASA partnerships. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark

item.title: La NASA quiere entender mejor la Luna antes de volver allí. Ha creado con IBM una IA para encontrar hielo y nuevos cráteres
item.description: Durante 17 años, la Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter ha fotografiado y medido la Luna hasta construir uno de los archivos más detallados que existen sobre su superficie. La NASA asegura que la misión ha generado un volumen de datos mayor que el de todas sus demás misiones planetarias combinadas , con una cobertura que permite observar buena parte del terreno lunar a gran resolución. El problema ya no es solo obtener información, sino procesarla con suficiente rapidez para extraer de ella patrones útiles. Y esa tarea gana peso mientras la agencia prepara el regreso de astronautas a la superficie… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Javier Marquez

item.title: Muscovite identified as a low-index building block for ultrathin van der Waals photonic components
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that a naturally occurring mineral can serve as a low-loss optical material for next-generation broadband all–van der Waals nanophotonic components. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ultrathin silicon structures can tune mid-IR light in billionths of a second
item.description: Light in the mid-infrared (mid-IR) portion of the electromagnetic spectrum plays a key role in modern sensing. Because molecules interact with this kind of light in specific ways, researchers use technologies like mid-IR spectroscopy to identify biological materials, drugs and pollutants. Mid-IR light can also serve as a carrier of information in free-space optical communications, where data are transmitted through the air without using cables or fibers. Better control of mid-IR light could therefore lead to more sensitive detectors and faster communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gondwana really was a supercontinent—and it may have helped kickstart life on Earth
item.description: Some 550 million years ago, Earth looked very different than it does today. The Southern Hemisphere was dominated by an enormous single continent known as Gondwana. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: River erosion explains uneven crustal uplift across Basque-Cantabrian Range
item.description: A University of the Basque Country-EHU research group has determined the causes of a 255 m (837 feet) crustal uplift of the Atlantic slope and a 167 m (548 feet) uplift of the Mediterranean slope, as well as the development of rivers in these areas. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fear-based education around porn is failing young people, study suggests
item.description: England's approach to teaching young people about pornography may be doing more harm than good, according to new research from the University of Surrey. A new study argues that fear-based education is failing to reflect how teenagers actually encounter sexual media. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chinese scientists boost hydrogen fuel cell power fourfold with new design
item.description: Chinese scientists have developed a way to generate a fourfold increase in power output of hydrogen fuel cells, an advance that could broaden their use from road vehicles to space missions. Hydrogen is widely viewed as a promising clean energy source for a low-carbon future. Fuel cells convert the chemical energy in hydrogen directly into electricity, producing water as their only exhaust. In a study published in the peer-reviewed journal Science on Thursday, researchers at the Beijing Institute... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: New pulse-train method aims to improve precision in quantum control
item.description: Quantum technologies are poised to transform fields ranging from medicine and sensing to computing and communications by manipulating the energy states of atoms and molecules. These manipulations are achieved by controlling quantum states with laser pulses. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 1,000 times faster operations bring reliable quantum computing a step closer
item.description: So far, quantum computers have been held back by their extreme sensitivity to errors and external disturbances. The longer a quantum operation takes, the greater the risk of computational errors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dead or alive, plankton support marine ecosystems
item.description: As tiny as they are, marine plankton play pivotal roles in biogeochemical cycles and sustaining aquatic ecosystems, producing around half of the oxygen on Earth and also acting as carbon sinks. When they die, their decomposing cells produce dissolved organic carbon that can be transformed and stored in the ocean for thousands of years, so understanding plankton mortality is essential for uncovering the mechanisms behind marine ecosystems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA, NFL Team Up to Showcase Space, Aeronautics Innovation
item.description: Through a new collaboration between NASA and the National Football League (NFL), the agency will soon bring America’s strengths in space exploration and aeronautics innovation to the football field. NASA will conduct flyovers, astronaut appearances, and fan engagement at NFL games across the United States as part of its new Inspiration Tour. “This is the […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Taveau

item.title: Navigating the social dynamics of sustainability
item.description: In the transformation toward sustainability, the interests of societal, economic and political actors often clash, making conflict inevitable. Understanding these dynamics and learning how to engage with them constructively is therefore crucial. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bringing hidden optical imperfections to light
item.description: Tiny manufacturing imperfections in optical components normally go unnoticed. Yet they can alter light in surprisingly significant ways. An international research team led by TU Darmstadt has shown that such imperfections can affect not only polarization—the direction in which light oscillates—but also the spatial shape of a light beam. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Continuous video of black hole radio observations challenges shock wave theory
item.description: For years, scientists have relied primarily on radio imaging from techniques like very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) to study jets from the active galactic nuclei of supermassive black holes. This allows for the detection of broad, unresolved features, called components, moving at what appear to be faster-than-light speeds. However, traditional imaging has poor resolution and treats each observation as a separate snapshot in time, limiting information about how the features move. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Injectable nanodevices could provide effective treatment for drug-resistant glioblastoma
item.description: Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant brain cancers known to medicine, carrying a median survival of just 12–15 months, even with the best available care. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Detecting 'pressure anisotropy' using zirconia nanoparticles
item.description: Researchers at University of Tsukuba have discovered that the crystal structure of zirconia nanoparticles remains stable under uniform pressure applied from all directions but changes under anisotropic pressure. This unique property is expected to lead to new technologies for detecting and evaluating pressure anisotropy, which has been difficult to assess using conventional methods. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Northern map turtles leave Lake Erie before algal blooms peak, tracking finds
item.description: Harmful algal blooms pose serious threats to people, animals and the environment. The University of Toledo's Dr. Jeanine Refsnider counts it as a positive discovery that northern map turtles tend to steer clear, as she and an undergraduate collaborator recently reported in the Journal of Great Lakes Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Disposable vapes pose hidden environmental threat, researchers warn
item.description: Vaping isn't just annoying to passersby who have to walk through clouds of vapor but may be actively harmful to the environment, a new study says. Discarded nicotine vapes contain extremely high levels of lead and other heavy metals in their remaining cache of e-liquid, researchers report in the journal Environmental Monitoring and Assessment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dust and Water in Sagittarius A*
item.description: A brilliant concentration of stars takes center stage in this Aug. 11, 2026, image taken by NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope. Webb observed IRS 3, a star near the end of its life cycle, located within this starfield. Webb’s mid-infrared data revealed the clear signature of oxygen-rich silicate dust, as well as, for the first […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: 'White graphene' reshaped at the atomic scale with tailor-made nanopores
item.description: A research team at the University of Vienna led by physicist Jani Kotakoski demonstrates how the shape of nanopores in hexagonal boron nitride—the electrically insulating counterpart to graphene, also known as "white graphene"—can be precisely controlled at the atomic level. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI is reshaping workplace, not replacing jobs, new research finds
item.description: Artificial intelligence is changing work in Ireland for the better, according to a new study led by Taha Yasseri, Workday Professor of Technology and Society at Trinity's School of Social Sciences & Philosophy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sun's largest sunspots may have potential to trigger superflares
item.description: The sun is capable of great things. In massive eruptions, it repeatedly hurls particles and radiation into space. This solar bombardment can be dangerous for technical infrastructure on Earth: For example, satellites and transformers in substations can be damaged. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: There's nothing irrational about resisting AI
item.description: If you read about AI, you'll find a widespread belief: When people don't want to use AI, it's because they're afraid or just don't understand it. They're afraid of losing their jobs or of change generally. Or they don't understand the technology, so they can't see the benefits. They're stuck in the past. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Article URL: https://gizmodo.com/this-nasa-color-trick-was-meant-for-mars-now-its-unveiling-rock-art-on-earth-2000809844 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49645437 Points: 210 # Comments: 34 Fuente: Hacker News - Portada.

item.title: Fossil flowers of ancient lianas preserved in amber reveal the evolution of tropical rainforests
item.description: Tiny flowers trapped in amber around 15 million years ago are offering scientists a rare glimpse into the plant life of a tropical rainforest in what is now Southeast China. Researchers have studied two exceptionally well-preserved fossil flowers from the Zhangpu flora. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Report maps pathways for accelerating environmental solutions through positive tipping points
item.description: New research from The Earthshot Prize and the University of Exeter's Green Futures Solutions team, published today, reveals 51 environmental solutions that can trigger rapid, transformative change to repair our planet within the next five years. After a northern summer of extreme heat and fire, and as the world prepares for an unprecedented El Niño, the research provides a new, unifying agenda for positive action. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Indonesia rescues six orangutans from fires in a week
item.description: Six orangutans including two nursing infants have been rescued from fires raging on Borneo island in the past week, Indonesian authorities and rescuers said on Thursday, bringing the total to 15 in a month. The apes were saved from plantations in deep rural West Kalimantan province, on the Indonesian part of the island, where they got stuck after fires cut off access to their forest home, according to the forestry ministry and the YIARI wildlife rehabilitation foundation. A large fire was... Publicado también por: South China Morning Post. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dangerous heat days are expanding beyond summer, with regional spring-fall shifts
item.description: Extreme heat has become more common—both research and lived experience document this—but when it arrives is a different question. A new study finds that, rather than occurring only during warm seasons, extreme heat events have become more frequent in the months before and after, too. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Peer-led computing camps engage children, study finds
item.description: High school student Khushi Kharuna creates and leads coding and artificial intelligence (AI) summer camps for K–12 students in her community outside Philadelphia. Priya Kumar, PNC Technologies Career Development Professor in Penn State's College of Information Sciences and Technology (IST), studies how young people navigate the digital world. Their shared interests led to a research collaboration exploring a youth-led STEM learning model that puts children's voices at the center of the learning experience. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Feather discovered in fossilised dinosaur poo is first of its kind
item.description: A well-preserved feather discovered inside fossilised dinosaur faeces could help explain why ancestors of modern birds survived the mass extinction. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Jacinta Bowler

item.title: A fossil feather preserved inside dinosaur poop could help explain why birds survived the mass extinction
item.description: About 66 million years ago, a dinosaur—maybe a T. rex or a Nanotyrannus—ate a bird. The record of that meal, in the form of fossilized poop, has survived to today, preserving the best example of a feather ever found from the age of dinosaurs. By studying this feather, scientists reported in a new study in the journal Current Biology, researchers have found clues that help explain why birds are the only group of dinosaurs that survived the mass extinction 66 million years ago. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists want to 3D print houses on Mars with the help of yeast
item.description: Mars is a terrible place to build a house. It's bitterly cold, blasted by radiation and a near vacuum. Not to mention that the building materials, even for a modest shelter, could spend months hurtling through space before construction begins. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: "¿Cómo podría la IA acabar realmente con todos nosotros?": 'El Mundo'
item.description: Lejos de un escenario como el de la película 'Terminator', expertos señalan que hay dos formas sobre cómo la inteligencia artifical podría acabar con la humanidad. Esto, luego de alertas por parte de investigadores de Anthropic. 'El Mundo' señala que los riesgos se dividen en dos categorias: perder el control de la IA y el mal uso por parte de los humanos. En su proceso por cumplir su objetivo, la inteligencia artificial podría ignorar el bienestar humano. Otro escenario podría ser más cercano a la película 'Wall-E', en la que los humanos ceden el control a las máquinas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Patricio Peralta

item.title: BepiColombo measures Mercury's particle bombardment up close
item.description: The joint BepiColombo mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) is settling into orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey. In early September, BepiColombo's two orbiters, the Mercury Planetary Orbiter and the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, separated from the transfer module. The orbiters will enter Mercury's orbit in November and separate from each other in December. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chinese cave traces Denisovan hunting and adaptation across 120,000 years
item.description: An ancient cave in southwestern China has revealed new evidence about how Denisovans—an ancient human relative—lived, survived and adapted over more than 100,000 years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Spinons may help electrons pair along stripes in some superconductors
item.description: Superconductors are materials that carry electricity with zero resistance below specific temperatures. Many of these materials become superconducting at very low temperatures, yet some enter superconducting phases at higher temperatures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How to support children during home relocation
item.description: As cost-of-living pressures increase and the rental crisis worsens, many families are moving more often. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A fake spider at the tip of this snake's tail helps it lure birds: Scientists get their first look inside it
item.description: Lots of animals use mimicry to survive. Some copy the appearance of threatening predators, and others have evolved to resemble plants or rocks so they can blend into the background and avoid being attacked. But a viper from Iran has found an even stranger strategy. The tip of this snake's tail looks like a spider, complete with a bulbous body and long dangling legs. And when a bird swoops in to try to eat this "spider," the snake springs into action and eats the bird. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Name our dino – ESA’s Hera asteroid mission mascot!
item.description: The European Space Agency’s Hera asteroid mission for planetary defence has a cartoon dinosaur for its mascot – because dinos were made extinct after an asteroid impact, but while they didn't have a space agency, people do! Now we’re asking you to supply our dino with a name , to win a place at November’s Hera arrival celebration. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Veterinarian outlines practical steps to protect pets from bird flu
item.description: As a veterinarian who studies infectious diseases in cats, I've been repeatedly asked whether Australia's outbreak of the H5 bird flu poses a risk to pets. The short answer is yes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hungry scent detection dogs more likely to 'cry wolf'
item.description: Dogs trained in scent detection may be better at sniffing out the right smell after breakfast, with new research finding hungry dogs working for treats are more likely to falsely identify the wrong scent. The study, led by researchers from the University of Waikato and Adelaide University, explored how meal timing affected dogs' accuracy in detecting target scents. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI watermarks may turn workplace praise and apologies into trust tests
item.description: Imagine a manager sends a thoughtful message to one of her hard-working employees after a particularly exhausting week in the office. The message communicates personal warmth, but when the recipient discovers it was generated by AI, it somehow feels less genuine. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Fingerprints' inside the sun could reveal if it once swallowed a planet
item.description: It is thought the sun may have engulfed a super-Earth-sized planet early in its history. Now, a new study has gone a step further, suggesting that such an event may have left behind detectable clues inside the sun that could still be visible today. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Australia's reading and math results are at an 'all‑time low'—but there's more to the story
item.description: Results from the latest international test of 15-year-olds have prompted another round of headlines suggesting there are serious problems with Australia's academic results. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mercury is shrinking more than we thought
item.description: Mercury's surface is riddled with wrinkles, evidence of a once-larger planet that has shrunk over time. A new study finds that Mercury may have contracted 10% to 30% more than previously thought—a loss of nearly 12 miles (19 kilometers) of total diameter since the planet formed—due to debris from impact craters obscuring signs of the planet's shrinking. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Agosto de 2026 fue el mes más caluroso jamás registrado en todo el planeta
item.description: Las temperaturas oceánicas también alcanzando niveles sin precedentes, informó el monitor climático europeo Copernicus. La ONU advirtió que el planeta continuará su avance a niveles nunca antes vistos hasta que la humanidad desista de los combustibles fósiles. Publicado también por: Clarín - Mundo. Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Von der Leyen: "Nuestra seguridad depende de la seguridad en el espacio"
item.description: La presidenta de la Comisión Europea defiende la creación de "un escudo espacial europeo" y Macron anticipa el primer alunizaje cien por cien europeo Leer Fuente: El Mundo - Internacional.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Fresneda

item.title: How two satellites are studying hurricanes during El Niño
item.description: In November 2025, NASA and its European partners launched the Sentinel-6B satellite to improve hurricane forecasts, help protect infrastructure and benefit commercial industries, including shipping. The satellite is now flying 30 seconds behind its predecessor, Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich. Both satellites are providing precise sea level height measurements during what oceanographers expect to be a historic El Niño, a naturally occurring oceanic phenomenon in which warmer-than-usual Pacific waters shift global weather patterns. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Peculiar' new species of Jurassic squid found in Wyoming
item.description: A "peculiar" new species of Jurassic squid-like animal has been unearthed in Wyoming, U.S., following the discovery of two exceptionally rare fossils dating to around 160 million years ago. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bulimba Creek tops Brisbane waterways for hazardous microplastics, risk analysis finds
item.description: A QUT investigation of the composition of microplastic types in three Brisbane creeks found that Bulimba Creek had a high load of hazardous microplastics. The work is published in the journal Marine Pollution Bulletin. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rib contouring highlights social media's role in reshaping body ideals and surgical interest
item.description: Rib contouring—a cosmetic procedure aimed at creating a smaller, more defined waist—is one of the newer appearance trends on social media. Influencers are sharing their experiences online, bringing a procedure many of us had probably never heard of into our social media feeds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scavenging linked to virus variety in wild birds
item.description: The scavenging behavior of many wild birds plays an important role in the type, number and variety of viruses they have, a new University of Otago–Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka-led study has found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A galaxy with almost no stars? New Cloud-9 observations strengthen the case
item.description: Astronomers have taken one of the deepest looks yet at Cloud-9, a candidate "dark galaxy," and found no trace of stars. The paper outlining this discovery was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Aug. 21. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First Nations ranger knowledge reveals the threats facing NT's green turtles
item.description: First Nations ranger groups working in protected areas such as national or marine parks have identified illegal commercial fishing as a major concern for the Northern Territory's green turtle populations, a study led by Charles Darwin University (CDU) and James Cook University (JCU) has found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: "Artemis II is done." Fuente: Ars Technica.

item.title: Amazon backs Ariane with rocket launch orders as Europe battles to close its space gap
item.description: The deal hands the continent's space industry a commercial boost as governments push for greater sovereign capabilities. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Kids face a cliff edge in independence that can affect mental health
item.description: As thousands of children start high school, experts have called for children to be given more opportunities for independence before they reach adolescence. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Yosemite's visitor surge revives concerns dating back 170 years
item.description: As the United States celebrates its 250th anniversary this summer, national parks are experiencing record-breaking visitation, with people flocking to enjoy the beauty and tranquility of the great outdoors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Seventeen minutes. On September 11, 2001, that was the length of time from when American Airlines Flight 11 crashed into the North Tower of the World... Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: AI pinpoints when fish reach their thermal limit
item.description: Researchers have developed an AI-based system that automatically and objectively detects the moment when fish experience loss of equilibrium (LOE) due to temperature stress. The system combines DeepLabCut, a deep-learning AI that captures animal posture from video, with ResNet34, a deep-learning AI-based image classification technology. Their system is expected to help predict the effects of climate change on fish. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: As oceans warm, Florida scientists hunt for heat-resistant coral
item.description: Off Florida's coast, a team of scientists and trained volunteers in scuba gear descends to the ocean floor, planting young coral onto a reef and examining how others are faring in increasingly warm waters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Online and undercover: Saving trafficked wildlife in Thailand
item.description: Nawee Changpirom has spent years working to rescue trafficked wildlife in Thailand, but even he can sometimes hardly believe the creatures he has found: leopards, hornbills and, once, an anteater. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Coyote density is 9 times higher in Seattle than in Washington's wildlands
item.description: Once coyotes get a taste for city living, the call of the wild fades to a whisper. Food is abundant and predators are few. Research indicates that coyotes enjoy the benefits of urban areas enough to put up with all the people, and Seattle is no exception. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Anthropic researcher resigns with warning about the dangers of AI development
item.description: An Anthropic researcher said he is resigning from the company over concerns the artificial intelligence firm and its competitors are not acting responsibly in AI development, echoing concerns raised inside and outside of the industry about the technology's potential to elude human control. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A stronger-than-normal El Nino alarms scientists over Galápagos wildlife and forests
item.description: The prediction that this season's El Niño phenomenon will be stronger than normal has alarmed the Ecuadorian scientific community, which has warned of its impact on the flora and fauna of the Galapagos Islands, home to the highest concentration of species not found elsewhere on Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In 2017, USGS released 72.57 kg of dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River; aircraft tracked it from above
item.description: In 2017, the US Geological Survey released 72.57 kg of Rhodamine WT dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River over 90 seconds to study how a tracer moves through flowing water. Researchers tracked the dye using instruments in the river and hyperspectral images captured from an aircraft flying 1,000 metres above the ground, with images recorded in 0.5-metre pixels across 48 spectral bands. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Gateshead uses 150m-deep mine water to heat 350 homes and public buildings
item.description: Water from deep beneath Gateshead now heats hundreds of homes and buildings. A six-megawatt heat pump extracts warmth from mine water, feeding a district network. This system, the largest of its kind in Great Britain, became operational in March 2023. Over five kilometers of pipes distribute the heated water to various public and private properties. Researchers are studying the mine water system through the Gateshead Living Laboratory. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists discover apple waste can remove up to 100% of lead from water
item.description: Researchers explored apple pomace for removing lead ions from contaminated water. Both raw and processed apple waste effectively removed lead from the solution. Extracted apple waste achieved complete lead removal under optimal experimental conditions. The biosorbents demonstrated rapid lead adsorption within the first hour of testing. These findings highlight apple pomace's potential for environmental remediation applications. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Fossil bones and tools from mysterious ancient human unearthed in China
item.description: A rare combination of tools and fossils found in a Chinese cave could help scientists learn more about our mysterious extinct cousins, the Denisovans. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Dust Storm Sweeps Over Mali
item.description: At a time of year when dust storm activity winds down, a plume of dust blanketed parts of the West African nation and its neighbors. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Timing 1080 drops to prevent predators bouncing back
item.description: While aerial 1080 drops sharply reduce numbers of rats and stoats, the predators—especially ship rats—can rebound to higher numbers within a few years. Studying 24 years of small-mammal tracking records across New Zealand's public conservation land, researchers found that the timing of these rebounds varies between regions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can AI tame torrential rain by 2050? The next frontier of weather control and forecasting
item.description: Japan has been experiencing increasingly severe damage from torrential rainfall triggered by typhoons and stationary linear rain bands. In response, an ambitious and unconventional idea is taking shape: artificially inducing heavy rainfall over the ocean to reduce extreme downpours on land. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI and big data can help logistics companies navigate supply-chain disruptions
item.description: Artificial intelligence and big-data capacity might help logistics companies withstand supply-chain disruptions by making them more agile and resilient, according to research in the International Journal of Business Performance and Supply Chain Modelling. The results are based on an analysis of responses from almost 300 logistics professionals in Indonesia. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Four in five researchers report harmful interactions during geoscience fieldwork. A new survey suggests a path forward.
item.description: Fieldwork is a vital part of geoscience research, allowing scientists and students to directly observe, interact with and collect data about Earth processes that cannot be replicated in the lab. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals the surface chemistry of bio-based hybrid materials
item.description: Just a few atomic layers at the surface can strongly influence how effectively a material binds pollutants from water or how efficiently a photocatalyst responds to light. Researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Polymer Research IAP use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to investigate the chemical states and interactions at the surfaces and interfaces of bio-based carbon materials and organic-inorganic hybrid materials. Their insights can support the targeted development of functional materials for future industrial applications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Luck or merit? Not all inequality is equally acceptable
item.description: Do you think it's fair that some people are better off financially than others? Does it perhaps matter whether those earnings stem from a lottery win or hard work? These are the kinds of questions economist Ingvild Almås of the University of Zurich is exploring. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The trapdoor spiders giving a leg up to science
item.description: WA's trapdoor spiders are endangered. Jackson Rendall is here to help—because he thinks they're "just really cool." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dementia prevention too heavily focused on personal choices, study finds
item.description: Efforts to prevent dementia may be placing too much responsibility on people's choices while overlooking the wider social and environmental conditions that shape brain health, a study has found. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
